title: The proper Hilbert functor of algebraic spaces is algebraic and locally finitely presented
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces and morphisms as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For morphisms of algebraic spaces, flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (the diagonal is quasi-compact); quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. A closed immersion of spaces is a representable morphism whose scheme base changes are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying topological spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $a:A\to B$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces over $S$. For a scheme $T\to B$, let $\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)$ be the set of closed subspaces $D\subset A\times_BT$ such that $D\to T$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Closed subspaces are identified when their closed immersions are isomorphic over the ambient space. Transition maps are inverse images of closed subspaces under base change. This functor is represented by an algebraic space $H\to B$ locally of finite presentation: there are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,H)\simeq\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)$ natural in every scheme $T\to B$. No properness or flatness of $A\to B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D01, quot-proposition-hilb; Hilbert functor in Tag 0CZY, quot-situation-hilb.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-hilbert-is-quot] to $a$. Its finite-presentation hypothesis holds. For every scheme $T\to B$ this identifies precisely the closed families of the statement with $\operatorname{Quot}_{\mathcal O_A/A/B}(T)$ via $D\mapsto(\mathcal O_{A_T}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_D)$, and its arbitrary-base-change compatibility identifies the transition maps as well.

source.place: Tag 0D01, quot-proposition-hilb, proof via Tags 0D00 and 09TU.

proof.text: The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_A$ is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation: on every etale chart it is free on one generator, with the presentation $\mathcal O^0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O\to0$. Thus [lem-sfb-space-quot-representability] applies with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_A$, since $a$ is separated and finitely presented. It provides an algebraic space $H\to B$ locally of finite presentation representing this Quot presheaf.

source.place: Tag 0D01, quot-proposition-hilb, proof via Tags 0D00 and 09TU.

proof.text: For each $T\to B$, compose the representing bijection of step 2 with the inverse of the bijection in step 1. This gives $\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,H)\simeq\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)$. For $g:T\prime\to T$, both component squares commute with the pullback along $g$, so their composite square commutes. The same $H\to B$ therefore represents the required functor and retains the local-finite-presentation property already proved in step 2.
